identity.description: Adobe Commerce, the e-commerce platform documented at developer.adobe.com/commerce. Two deployment types with different API surfaces: PaaS (Adobe Commerce on Cloud / on-premises) and SaaS (Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service).
identity.identity_notes: The developer.adobe.com/commerce pages document the Adobe Commerce REST, GraphQL and SOAP APIs, matching the requested product. The Magento-to-Adobe Commerce naming lineage was not quoted from a fetched page.

auth.oauth_flows: No OAuth 2.0 flow found. The documented OAuth option is OAuth 1.0a for third-party integrations, categorized here as Other.
auth.token_refresh: unknown. The auth page does not state token expiry or refresh. Session cookies expire after inactivity, with the timeout not stated.
auth.scopes_notes: Access is limited to the resources selected when an integration is created in Admin (System > Extension > Integration). Admin and customer tokens are limited to what that user's role or the customer's own data allows.

access.production_restrictions: No app-review gate for publishing was found in the sources reviewed. A search snippet (not fetched) says Adobe Commerce extension submissions (EE) require a partner account or a developer license.

api.limitations: The 'wide range' claim applies to PaaS. SaaS gets a smaller REST subset, and SaaS excludes the customer and guest REST APIs. Specific resource names and write-method details were not confirmed from the fetched pages. Rate limits, webhooks and SDKs are not established.

open_questions: Token expiry and refresh behavior for integration and admin tokens is not stated in the sources reviewed.
Rate limits, webhooks/events and official SDKs were not established. The webhooks page returned 404.
Whether a non-partner developer can get free test credentials (for example, a self-hosted Magento Open Source install) was not confirmed for Adobe Commerce. Snippets conflict.
The App Builder MCP server's owner repository and its data access (REST API vs docs only) were not located.
The free account and developer license claims come from search snippets that were not fetched.

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Credentials require partnership, vendor approval or sales.
